text: If a company can email you your password, run. If a company can email you your password, run. Let me show you what should actually happen when you sign up. The naive way: store your password in a table as plain text. One database leak and every account is wide open, and people reuse passwords everywhere. So we never store the password. We run it through a one-way hash function, easy to compute forwards, basically impossible to reverse. But hackers precompute rainbow tables of common passwords. So we add a salt, a random string mixed and hacked before hashing. So we add a salt, a random string mixed in before hashing unique per user. Now identical passwords get different hashes and precomputed tables are useless. Slow hashes like bcrypt. Slow hashes like bcrypt make brute force painful too. Good apps don't store your password. They store a riddle only you can answer. Next episode, we'll talk about how Netflix loads instantly
